advances: Physical planar component records at a finite menu of slopes, with the source already at the maximum of its concave profile.

proof:
The two arms are continuous, concave and nonincreasing by the closed superlevel description in 0586b032c888ffb0. They are nonnegative because $r(0)=R$, and their values at zero are positive. For an arm $A$ and a selected $s>0$, put $a_s=\max\{v\in[0,R]:A(v)\ge sv\}$. It is positive, and $A-sv$ is strictly decreasing. If $a_s<R$ it satisfies $A(a_s)=sa_s$. Otherwise $A(R)\ge sR$.

Partition each arm at its distinct internal $a_s$. At an internal grid point both inward derivatives are finite by finite concavity on a neighborhood of the point. At zero the initial right derivative is bounded above by zero by nonincrease and below by any chord slope to a later point, so it too is finite. Use the internal part of the local curvature-replacement lemma on every nonterminal cell, and its terminal part on the last cell. For $m\ge2$ take $w(v)=v^{m-2}$. It is continuous on every cell and strictly positive in its interior. For $m=1$ take $w=1$. Thus for $m\ge2$ the preserved records on each cell are $\int v^{m-2}A$, $\int v^{m-1}A$ and $\int v^{m-2}A^2$, and for $m=1$ they include $\int A$.

The replacement fixes all internal grid values and the two values $A_\pm(0)$. At each interior join the new derivative from the left is at least the original left derivative, which is at least the original right derivative, which is at least the new derivative from the right. The assembled arm is therefore continuous, concave and nonincreasing. The last value can increase only at the completed top. The internal $a_s$ remain the same by the fixed equality and strict decrease, and a top-saturated $a_s=R$ remains so by the terminal inequality. Each of at most $q+1$ cells contributes at most eight curvature locations, and there are at most $q$ original internal grid points, giving the stated conservative count.

To verify the records, use the exact physical component kernels of 0586b032c888ffb0. On the nonnegative arm the outer branch applies for $0<v<a_s$ and the inner branch for $a_s<v<R$. Endpoints are null for the level integrals. Integrating the accepted $c_s$ gives
$$
C_s(A)=\frac{a_s^m}{2}+\frac{m-1}{2s}\int_{a_s}^R v^{m-2}A(v)\,dv.
$$
The integrals of $k_s$ and $j_s$ in that fact are respectively $K_s(A)-sR^{m+1}/4$ and $J_s(A)+sR^{m+1}/4$, where
$$
\begin{aligned}
K_s(A)&=\frac{s a_s^{m+1}}4+\frac{m-1}{4s}\int_{a_s}^R v^{m-2}A(v)^2\,dv,\\
J_s(A)&=\frac m2\int_0^{a_s} v^{m-1}A(v)\,dv-\frac{s a_s^{m+1}}4
+\frac{m-1}{4s}\int_{a_s}^R v^{m-2}A(v)^2\,dv .
\end{aligned}
$$
The constants follow by integrating the inner-branch terms $\mp s(m+1)v^m/4$. They cancel between the arms in the differences giving $M(s)$ and $P(s)-V/2$. The total coarea is $C_s(A_+)+C_s(A_-)$. The recorded moments and the fixed intersections preserve all these quantities and each arm volume. When $m=1$ every term with $m-1$ is omitted, and $\int A$ together with the fixed intersections suffices. At $s=0$, $P(0)$ is the positive arm volume and $M(0)=0$. The section at $z=0$ runs from $-R$ to $R$ with constant density $R^{m-1}/2$, so each of its two half-sections has mass $R^m/2$. This proves the zero-slope assertions directly.

Finally the set of $(z,v)$ with $0\le v\le R$ and $-\widehat A_-(v)\le z\le\widehat A_+(v)$ is a compact convex polygon. Its horizontal intervals are nested by nonincrease. Its top boundary as a function of $z$ is therefore a concave piecewise affine profile. Because the arms are positive at zero and nonnegative at the top, the chord inequality makes both positive for $v<R$; the new profile has positive interior and maximum $R$ at zero. The fixed zero-level endpoints give the original axial interval. The closed polygon also gives continuity of the top profile at both endpoints: compactness gives the upper bound by its endpoint value on any limit from the interior, and concavity gives the matching lower bound by chords from the endpoint. A horizontal arm segment corresponds to a vertical side face, and positive top values allow a plateau. These constructions preserve the stated finite records in the original physical density law for each profile.

statement: Let $m\ge1$ be an integer and $r$ a continuous nonnegative concave profile on a compact interval $[a,b]$, with $a<0<b$ and $r(0)=\max r=R>0$. For $v\in[0,R]$, write the closed superlevel interval as $[-A_-(v),A_+(v)]$. On the planar region $|x|\le r(z)$, $z\in[a,b]$, give Lebesgue measure the density $r(z)^{m-1}/2$. Let $P(s)$ be the mass of $z+sx\ge0$, and $C(s),M(s)$ the integrals of the density and $z$ times the density on $z+sx=0$, with line measure divided by $\sqrt{1+s^2}$. For any list of $q$ finite positive slopes there is a continuous piecewise affine concave profile $\widehat r$ on the same interval with $\widehat r(0)=R$ and at most $9(q+1)$ curvature locations per inverse arm. The replacement preserves both arm volumes $m\int_0^R v^{m-1}A_\pm(v)\,dv$ and each selected $P(s),C(s),M(s)$, also at $s=0$. The zero-slope coarea is $R^m/2$ per arm and $R^m$ in total, and $M(0)=0$. Outer endpoint heights can be zero, and the maximum can be a plateau.
title: Finite-knot replacement preserving physical profile cap records
